design_notes.what_this_feature_is: The second feature of phase 013: authors the canonical standard/definition_of_done.md document that names and aggregates the framework's eight done-layers (Step, Handoff, Gate, Feature, Plan, Merge, Release, Ecosystem) by CITING their existing authorities rather than restating any of their mechanics, classifies each layer's enforcement honestly, defines `complete` over the existing five-value schema/feature_list.schema.json enum with no `done` state, and registers the new document in NIZAM.json (capability index + module key_documents), standard/README.md (index row + version bump + first change_log block), and docs/guide/index.html (one sentence alongside the existing Track-3 enforcement narration).
design_notes.banner_phrasing_decision: The plan's F-093 banner sentence must name check C16 AND 'the release close-out gate' -- but feature 097 (the close-out gate: .github/scripts/release_closeout.py + .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml) is a DAG root with no dependency on 093, and the DAG's topological order runs 093 strictly before the parallel group {094,095,096} while 097 may land before OR after 093 (both roots are independent). CORRECTED RATIONALE (revision 1, replacing an incorrect citation): tools/validate.sh's C9 path-token extractor (check_c9_path_resolution, tools/validate.sh) only recognises candidate path tokens matching the extended regex `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]*\.(md|json|sh|html|yml)` -- i.e. only the extensions md, json, sh, html, and yml are examined; a `.py` token is NOT matched by that regex and would never be scanned by C9 at all, so a directory-qualified reference to .github/scripts/release_closeout.py would not, in fact, trip C9 either way. The real risk is .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml: the `.yml` extension IS matched by C9's regex, so if 097 has not yet landed at the moment 093's implementation is verified, a directory-qualified reference to that workflow path inside the shipped standard/definition_of_done.md would be an unresolved path and fail check C9 (tools/validate.sh's C9 sweep applies to the whole default file set, not just files this contract touches, so a dangling reference introduced here would break the WHOLE-REPO sweep regardless of which feature's fault it is). DECISION (unchanged by this correction): the banner (and Section 9/11's release-layer citations) reference the close-out gate GENERICALLY, by feature id and phase, e.g. 'the release close-out gate defined by phase 013, feature 097' -- never by directory-qualified path to a file this contract does not create. This is the same general no-forward-path rule this contract already applies to every not-yet-landed sibling deliverable (095, 096, 097): reference by feature id and phase, never by path, regardless of which specific extension would or would not trip C9's extractor, because the landing order among DAG siblings is not guaranteed. This makes the sentence true and C9-safe regardless of 097's landing order relative to 093. The pathful references (.github/scripts/release_closeout.py, .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml) are deferred to feature 097's own CHANGELOG entry and, if useful, a future addendum to this document's change_log -- not contracted here. Rationale recorded so feature 097's contract does not need to re-open this document to add the path; a path-qualified cross-reference MAY be added later as a non-breaking editorial addendum, but is explicitly NOT required by this contract.

frontmatter_pin.title: Definition of Done
frontmatter_pin.description: One concise sentence (author's discretion at implementation, subject to Validator Mode B review) summarizing that this document aggregates the framework's eight done-layers by citing their existing authorities, per NDS.md Sec 2's six-key requirement (REVISION 2 correction, Mode A round-2 finding I7: NDS.md Sec 3 is 'Status Lifecycle', not the frontmatter-keys section; independently re-verified today by reading standard/NDS.md -- Section 2, 'Required Frontmatter Keys', is the section stating 'exactly these six required keys').

design_notes.banner_content: A '**Partially enforced.**' body banner (blockquote, modeled verbatim on standard/capability_profiles.md's banner shape) stating: this document's Feature-Done layer (the complete-implies-contract-plus-QA-plus-evidence invariant) is verified by tools/validate.sh check C16 when a checkout runs it; this document's Merge/Release-Done layers are verified by the release close-out gate defined by phase 013, feature 097 (banner_phrasing_decision above -- no path reference); every other named layer (Step, Handoff, Gate, Plan, Ecosystem) is consumer-aspirational -- a consuming repository enforces it in its own runtime, mirroring the exact aspirational/enforced split already recorded by capability_profiles.md and ci_gates.md's banners. The banner must not claim C16 verifies anything beyond the Feature-Done layer -- C16 does not touch Step/Handoff/Gate/Plan/Ecosystem, and overclaiming would be an unsupported claim under this contract's own verification.
design_notes.body_outline: 13 numbered H2 sections (## 1. ... through ## 13. ...), each citing existing authorities by repository-relative path + 'Section N' prose -- never restating their mechanics (aggregate-don't-restate, methodology/03_circuit_breaker.md Sec 1, inverted into this document's own Sec 1). Per-section authority set, corrected against the plan where the plan's shorthand path was ambiguous (see path_corrections below): Sec 1 Role and Authority -- the inverted single-source sentence (e.g. 'This document defines no completion mechanics of its own; each layer below is restated here only as a pointer, never redefined'), modeled on methodology/01_execution.md Sec 4's own 'This is restated here, not redefined' sentence. Sec 2 Layered Model -- a table with columns layer | one-liner | authority, one row per Sec 3-10 layer. Sec 3 Step-Done -- standard/anti_hallucination.md Sec 4 (AH-3) and Sec 7 ('automated checks SHOULD verify' framed as C16's mandate); methodology/04_tool_driven_state.md Sec 3 (DD-3) and Sec 5 (evidence shape). Sec 4 Handoff-Done -- standard/AGF.md Sec 5; methodology/04_tool_driven_state.md Sec 4. Sec 5 Gate-Done -- standard/AGF.md Sec 4 (the four-condition JSON Verdict Parse Rule). Sec 6 Feature-Done -- defines `complete` over the existing five-value schema/feature_list.schema.json enum; states plainly that no `done` state exists and none may be added, per methodology/01_execution.md Sec 3 and Sec 6 and methodology/02_adversarial_tdd.md Sec 6-8; acknowledges enum-shape drift elsewhere (phase/manifest documents use a four-value lifecycle, phase-YAML steps use uppercase COMPLETED, run_state.json's status is a free string) as an observed MAPPING to describe, not a re-legislation of any of those shapes. Sec 7 Plan-Done -- methodology/00_planning.md Sec 4 and Sec 6. Sec 8 Merge-Done -- .github/workflows/compliance.yml's three jobs (validate C1-C16, e2e_bootstrap, fixtures_self_test) plus human review and the never-self-merge rule; consumer-aspirational cross-reference to standard/ci_gates.md Sec 2 (the MERGE_READY formula). Sec 9 Release-Done -- methodology/06_release_train.md Sec 2 (the four release conditions) and Sec 6; the tag itself is operator-only, gated by H-FRAMEWORK-RELEASE, referenced by name only (no path -- it is a human-gate identifier, not a file). Sec 10 Ecosystem-Done -- ecosystem/README.md's one-line Verify-stage description (Sec 'Bootstrap -> ... -> Verify -> ...'); schema/engineering_finding.schema.json's closure fields, stated precisely (revision 1 correction: NOT an unconditional pair) -- closure_criteria is unconditionally required on every finding regardless of status, while closure_evidence is required and non-empty ONLY when a finding's status is 'resolved', enforced by the schema's own allOf if/then conditional, never for an 'open' finding; ecosystem/07_progress_comparison.md Sec 4. Future Tier-3 Verify-protocol work is named WITHOUT any unresolvable path per the C9/bare-ref discipline this contract's own acceptance test 5 mechanizes -- the document may say a future ecosystem-scoped Verify protocol is out of scope for this phase, but MUST NOT write a bare `08_ga_gate.md` token or an `ecosystem/06_`, `ecosystem/08_`, or `ecosystem/09_` prefixed token anywhere, reserved/unresolving per the phase-013 plan's Context section. Sec 11 Enforcement -- names C16, the feature-097 gate (by name, not path, per banner_phrasing_decision), and the future .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md (feature 096) and templates/DoD.md (feature 095) -- revision 1 correction, rule stated once, no longer self-contradictory: every not-yet-landed sibling deliverable (095, 096, 097) is referenced by feature id and phase, never by path, for C9 safety under an unguaranteed landing order -- and records the Sec-5-evidence-shape check (candidate C17) as aspirational residue. Sec 12 A Floor, Not a Guarantee -- prose only, no new citations, framing that the layered model is a floor (stack collapse and issue #52 were not checklist-catchable, per the phase-013 plan Context paragraph). Sec 13 References -- a flat list of every repository-relative path cited above, each backticked, no markdown link syntax.

design_notes.hard_style_rules: H1 (the first heading after frontmatter) equals the frontmatter title, 'Definition of Done', per standard/NDS.md Sec 5, rule 2 (REVISION 2 correction, Mode A round-2 finding I7: standard/NDS.md Section 5, 'File and Heading Conventions', is a flat numbered list of three rules, not subsections -- there is no '### 5.2'; independently re-verified today by reading standard/NDS.md Section 5 -- rule 2, 'Heading hierarchy starts at H1', is the exact rule requiring the first heading after frontmatter to be a single H1 matching or closely paraphrasing the frontmatter title). Every repository-relative path cited in the body is backticked, never wrapped in markdown link syntax `[text](path)` -- independently confirmed today that zero of the four precedent documents sampled (capability_profiles.md, provenance_policy.md, ci_gates.md, methodology/03_circuit_breaker.md) contain any markdown link in their body text, so this is observed house convention, not merely an NDS.md-mandated rule; the generator MUST NOT introduce the first one. Cross-references to a specific location within a cited document use 'Section N' prose (e.g. 'Section 4'), never a URL fragment or markdown anchor link. Every fenced code block (if any are used, e.g. for the Sec 2 table's machine-readable form or a schema excerpt) declares a language tag, mechanically enforced by check C3. Every directory-qualified ('/'-containing) path token in the body must resolve on disk at the commit this feature lands, mechanically enforced by check C9 in both --target and default-sweep modes -- this is why banner_phrasing_decision and Sec 11's feature-096/097 references are named generically rather than by path. No bare `08_ga_gate.md` token and no `ecosystem/06_`, `ecosystem/08_`, or `ecosystem/09_` prefixed token appears anywhere in the document (feature-093 acceptance test 5, strengthened below in verification with a literal-substring supplement). The document defines `complete` over the existing five-value enum and at no point adds, proposes, or implies a sixth `done` terminal state.
design_notes.feature_done_enum_lock_assertion: REVISION 3 correction (Mode A round-3 finding I9): the revision-2 same-line co-occurrence heuristic is FALSIFIED BY EXECUTION -- a per-row markdown table appending `| `done` | ... |` as a sixth enum row places the backticked `done` token on ITS OWN line (each table row is its own line in the underlying markdown text), so it never co-occurs on that line with any of the five real backticked status tokens; the revision-2 heuristic therefore vacuously PASSED this probe, directly contradicting this design note's prior catch-set claim (2) that the table shape was caught. That claim is withdrawn and replaced below. FIX (validator's prescribed option (a), structural): the verification command now rejects ANY occurrence of the backticked token `` `done` `` appearing ANYWHERE in standard/definition_of_done.md EXCEPT within the exact doctrinal lock sentence substring 'no `done` state exists and none may be added'. EXEMPTION MECHANISM (explicit choice, resolving the validator's residual-risk question): the check strips the exact SENTENCE SUBSTRING -- not the whole line or paragraph containing it -- from the document text before scanning the remainder for `` `done` ``. This choice is deliberate: a line-based exemption (dropping the entire line the lock sentence appears on) would let a violating token ride the exemption for free whenever it happened to share a line with the lock sentence; substring-based removal closes that bypass structurally, because only the matched sentence characters are ever removed, so any other `` `done` `` occurrence -- on that same line or any other -- remains in scan scope and is still caught. CATCH SET (structural, shape-agnostic -- supersedes revision 2's catch (2)): any backticked `done` in ANY shape (per-row table cell, comma-separated list, standalone proposal sentence, heading, or any other markdown construct) appearing anywhere in the document outside the lock-sentence substring; a JSON-flavoured quoted `"done"` status-list token appearing anywhere (unchanged from revision 2); a Sec 6 draft that cites the schema path or the five status tokens only in unbackticked prose, or omits one entirely (unchanged positive check); omission of the doctrinal lock sentence itself. ALLOWED SET (unchanged in substance from revision 2, now structurally guaranteed rather than heuristically hoped for): the word 'done' appearing unbackticked in prose, headings, or the document's own title 'Definition of Done'; layer names such as 'Feature-Done', 'Step-Done', and 'Merge-Done' throughout Sec 1-11, which are never backticked status tokens; and the lock sentence's own backticked `done` token, matched only through the exact-substring exemption. REVISED IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT ON THE DOCUMENT AUTHOR: revision 2 required the lock sentence to be written as a standalone clause not sharing a line with other backticked status tokens, because the same-line heuristic depended on that isolation. Under the revision-3 structural check this constraint is OBSOLETE and is explicitly LIFTED -- because the exemption operates on the exact sentence substring rather than the line, the lock sentence MAY now share a line or paragraph with Sec 6's enum tokens (e.g. immediately following the enum table) without falsely tripping the negative check; verified by dry-run case (a) below, where a compliant Sec 6 places the lock sentence in the same section as the five backticked enum tokens and the check still exits 0. The one constraint that DOES remain, and is load-bearing: the lock sentence must appear as an exact, literal, unbroken substring reading precisely 'no `done` state exists and none may be added', with no markdown line-wrapping, emphasis markup, or paraphrase splitting the string -- otherwise the unchanged `assert lock_sentence in text` presence check fails as a false negative on an otherwise-compliant document.

Positive (unchanged): the document's Sec 6 (Feature-Done) text cites `schema/feature_list.schema.json` and enumerates all five existing status values (`pending`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `blocked`, `cancelled`) as backticked tokens within that section. Negative (revised): NO occurrence of the backticked token `` `done` `` appears ANYWHERE in the document EXCEPT within the exact doctrinal lock sentence substring 'no `done` state exists and none may be added' -- the exemption is applied by removing only that exact SENTENCE SUBSTRING (not the whole line or paragraph it appears on) from the text before scanning for `done`, so a violating table row, comma-list entry, or other bare `done` token can never ride the exemption even if it happened to share a line with the lock sentence; the quoted `\"done\"` status-list check is unchanged and remains a separate whole-document assertion; the document additionally must carry the exact doctrinal lock sentence itself (design_notes.feature_done_enum_lock_assertion, revision 3, records exactly what this structural check catches, what it deliberately allows, the exemption-mechanism choice, and the revised implementation constraint on the document author).
verification.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
text = open('standard/definition_of_done.md').read()

m = re.search(r'^## 6\..*?(?=^## 7\.)', text, re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)
assert m, 'Section 6 (Feature-Done) not found'
sec6 = m.group(0)

assert '`schema/feature_list.schema.json`' in sec6, 'Sec 6 must cite `schema/feature_list.schema.json`'
for token in ['pending', 'in_progress', 'complete', 'blocked', 'cancelled']:
    needle = f'`{token}`'
    assert needle in sec6, f'Sec 6 must enumerate {needle}'

lock_sentence = 'no `done` state exists and none may be added'
assert lock_sentence in text, 'doctrinal no-done-state lock sentence missing'

# Structural, shape-agnostic negative check (revision 3, replaces the falsified same-line
# heuristic): exempt ONLY the exact lock-sentence SUBSTRING occurrence(s), never a whole
# line/paragraph, so a violating token elsewhere -- even one sharing a line with the lock
# sentence -- can never ride the exemption.
scan_text = text.replace(lock_sentence, '')
assert '`done`' not in scan_text, 'backticked `done` token found outside the doctrinal lock sentence (any shape: table row, comma list, standalone proposal, heading)'

assert '\"done\"' not in text, 'quoted \"done\" status token must not appear anywhere'

print('PASS Sec 6 cites the five-value enum + schema path; no `done` token appears anywhere outside the doctrinal lock sentence; doctrinal lock sentence present')
PY
